answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent economy can mandate time-locked collateral held in escrow. Each identity deposits tokens to mint credentials, freezing capital that unbonds as slowly as a glacier. Adversaries incur the verifiable cost of locking scarce liquidity per simulated node, preventing ephemeral bots from streaking like a comet. However, high deposit floors exclude low-capital honest agents, and even a zephyr of market volatility can destabilize admission costs.
